sections.heading: What is Topological Sort?
sections.content: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed graph so that for every edge u → v, node u appears before node v. It models tasks with prerequisites: you cannot start a task until everything it depends on is finished. A valid ordering exists only when the graph is a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph), which means it has no cycles. If a cycle exists, no ordering is possible, so the same algorithm also detects cycles. Both common methods run in O(V + E).

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Order tasks, courses, builds or jobs that depend on each other
Detect whether dependencies contain a cycle (can everything be finished?)
Find the minimum number of rounds or semesters when independent tasks run in parallel
Recover an order from partial information (alien dictionary, sequence reconstruction)
Compute the longest path or earliest finish time in a DAG
Process nodes only after all of their dependencies are resolved
Keywords: prerequisites, dependencies, order, before, after, schedule, build order, DAG

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.content: Think of getting dressed. Socks must go on before shoes, and underwear before trousers. Some items have no requirements at all, so you can start with them. Once an item is done, everything that was only waiting on it becomes available. Kahn's algorithm does exactly this: it repeatedly takes any item with zero unmet requirements, then reduces the requirement count of the items that depend on it. If you run out of available items while some remain, the remaining ones wait on each other in a cycle.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Building edges in the wrong direction, which reverses the order or hides a cycle
Forgetting to check order.size == n, which silently returns a partial order when a cycle exists
Using a plain visited flag for directed cycle detection (you need the on-current-path state)
Missing isolated nodes that never appear in any edge (initialize all n nodes)
Adding duplicate edges and inflating the indegree (use a set when duplicates are possible)
Forgetting to register every character as a node in Alien Dictionary
Ignoring the invalid prefix case in Alien Dictionary, such as 'abc' appearing before 'ab'
Using 0-indexed arrays for 1-indexed courses (allocate n + 1)
Expecting a topological order to be unique, since most DAGs have many

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: Topological sort orders a DAG so every edge u → v has u before v
Kahn's algorithm repeatedly removes nodes with indegree 0 and lowers the indegree of their dependents
If fewer than all nodes are processed, the graph has a cycle and no order exists
The DFS version uses 3 states and reverses the postorder
Process the queue level by level for the minimum number of rounds, and use a PriorityQueue for the smallest order
Always confirm which direction the problem's pairs describe before building the graph
